description:
Bitcoin Cost Basis Distribution on one date: how the unspent BTC supply is spread across price levels, where a coin's level is its cost basis (the BTC price on the day it last moved on-chain). Computed exactly from the UTXO set for the date with the bins you choose.
Returns a compact summary: date, BTC price of the date, total supply, supply in profit / in loss / at breakeven (BTC and %), unpriced genesis-era coins, the bin holding the price, the largest level below and above the price (on-chain support / resistance), the top N levels, and the access block. The bin array is returned only with include_bins (non-empty bins only).
Defaults: latest date, 50 logarithmic bins over the full cost basis range. Use price_min/price_max to zoom (supply outside goes to out_of_range).
Access: Free on any date. Free/demo keys: top ≤ 10, at most 10 calls per minute and 30 different past dates per hour (200 per day); the latest date is not counted. Pro: no date quota. For the history of the distribution over time use render_chart with heatmap_id "cost-basis-distribution".

date.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Omit for the latest available date.

include_bins.description: Also return the non-empty bins with % and cumulative %.

price_max.description: Upper bound of the bin range, USD (0.0001…1e9). Kept as given; with one bound only, the other side comes from the data (error if no cost basis lies on that side).

price_min.description: Lower bound of the bin range, USD (0.0001…1e9; 0 allowed for linear only). Kept as given.

scale.description: "log" (default, geometric bins) or "linear" (equal-width bins from 0 or price_min).

name: get_cbd_snapshot
